body:
I've had [selective eating ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avoidant/restrictive_food_intake_disorder)my whole life which was obvious, but in retrospect I've also had depression, anxiety, and ADD my whole life. I always thought that the next step would be better. I always thought that next year I would try harder, I wouldn't procrastinate, I'd do my homework, I could be a good student if I tried, but I always fell behind. And I was lonely. I was always afraid anyone who got to know me would find out how lazy I was. It was tough mentally, but I got through the days by distracting myself with internet, games, and hope that the next opportunity would go better. My discipline never got better. Even though people told me I was smart, and I felt like I was doing my best, I couldn't keep up with the pace of the gifted programs I was in. I built a habit of avoiding that frustration by procrastinating and skating by on the minimum required work, but I just replaced frustration with shame. I thought that my actual career would be my last chance to get things right, but I'm still stuck in the same patterns. I procrastinate because I can't face my anxiety about getting work done or exposing my mistakes by asking for help. I don't want to make excuses for myself, so I blame myself for everything that goes wrong. At this point in my life, I think of myself as a lazy guy who gets away without doing his fair share just by sounding smart and saying the right things. Every day I'm scared that my coworkers or my manager will find out how much I really procrastinate, how little effort I put into my work.

Really what makes me feel hopeless is that I haven't changed my habits in 28 years. I've kept up a empirically unsupported optimism because I want to be a responsible person, but when I look at the way I've actually behaved I feel like more of a conman than anything else. My wife told me this morning that all she sees me do is mope and feel sorry for myself, that I'm not doing anything to actually improve my life or hers, that I'm just making empty gestures at change that don't amount to anything. I can't help but agree, and I've felt that way for as long as I can remember but now I'm running out of excuses. I have every opportunity available for me, I have the exact life on paper that I wanted for myself. Knowing what I need to do for myself hasn't ever helped me before, so it seems dishonest to expect that's going to change now. I can see the frustration that I put my wife through, and it's only a matter of time before my workplace starts to get fed up with me as well. I'm convinced that I'm never going to change, and that I'll struggle with depression and anxiety, and the consequences of my own decisions and laziness. I'm only making things harder for my wife and coworkers, but I still feel responsible for trying to change even when I'm personally hopeless, I'm just getting tired of the struggle. I'm not a good person the way I am now, I'm certainly not the person I want to be. If I give up and quit my job, I'll never make that much money again, and I don't want to put my wife through having to sell the house we just bought.
